Fact.Name: Gambling activities carried on as a trade or business
Fact.Description:
Return-level classification for 2025. If this is a joint return, did either you or your spouse engage in gambling activities as a trade or business (professional gambling), rather than as personal or recreational gambling? On a non-joint return, classify the filer's gambling activity. Do not infer the answer from the size or frequency of winnings.
Ask whenever this return reports gambling winnings or gambling losses, whether or not a Form W-2G was issued. Answer Yes when either person covered by this return carried on gambling as a trade or business. Yes blocks this return because the current graph has no gambling Schedule C activity, Schedule SE tax, or business-expense application of the 2018-2025 IRC 165(d) wagering rule. No keeps the existing nonbusiness Schedule 1 line 8b and Schedule A treatment.
No safe answer is inferred from silence. The writable stays Incomplete if unanswered; the guard below is complete-safe false when no answer is present so returns with no W-2G intake keep their existing graph values. This posture is safe only with the application handoff: the application requires the answer whenever this return reports gambling winnings or losses, including amounts not on Form W-2G. For a joint return, the classification covers either spouse. An unanswered question is not evidence that the gambling was not a trade or business.

Fact.Name: Gambling trade or business needs Schedule C and Schedule SE
Fact.Description: An answered Yes refuses submission because this dictionary reports gambling winnings on Schedule 1 line 8b and has no Schedule C gambling activity, Schedule SE tax computation, or IRC 165(d) cap on business expenses. A No answer does not change a number. An unanswered classification is read as false here to preserve the existing complete-safe graph. This posture is safe only with the application handoff: the application requires an answer whenever gambling winnings or losses are reported. This refusal does not compute the Schedule C, Schedule SE, or business-expense limit.

Fact.Name: Forms W-2G
Fact.Description: Form W-2G: Certain Gambling Winnings — one collection item per W-2G the payer issued. This models the two boxes the 1040 consumes (box 1 reportable winnings; box 4 federal income tax withheld); the wager-type/date/payer detail boxes are not modeled.

Fact.Name: W-2G box 1 — reportable winnings
Fact.Description: Form W-2G box 1: reportable gambling winnings for this W-2G. Flows (via /w2gWinnings) to Schedule 1 line 8b gambling income.

Fact.Name: W-2G box 4 — federal income tax withheld
Fact.Description: Form W-2G box 4: federal income tax withheld on these winnings (regular or backup withholding). Flows (via /w2gWithholding) to Form 1040 line 25c.

Fact.Name: State
Fact.Description:
Form W-2G box 13, State/Payer’s state: the state this gambling winning was reported to.
This is the writable optional fact. Can be left incomplete. Please use the derived fact ../state in downstream calculations. No federal fact reads it: the box is a state key and the federal return has no use for which state a payer withheld for. It exists so the answer can be written down rather than refused, and handed to a state system.

Fact.Name: State
Fact.Description:
Alias for writableState to avoid breaking our backend with our convention for optional fields. Form W-2G box 13, State/Payer’s state.
THE EXPORTED SHAPE, copied from interest:/interestReports/*/state (dictionary/ty2025/interest.xml): the writable stays private and optional and the derived alias carries the state-systems export, so a state system reads one path name on every income collection in this dictionary.
UNANSWERED IT IS INCOMPLETE, which is the interest alias's behaviour exactly. A state identity has no safe default: constants:/incomeFormStateOptions has two members, sameState and differentState, and neither of them means "not answered".
THE FEDERAL RETURN READS NOTHING FROM THIS FACT. It is export-only on the federal side and no federal line moves with it.

Fact.Name: State income tax withheld
Fact.Description:
Form W-2G box 15, the state income tax withheld on this gambling winning.
This is the writable optional fact. Can be left incomplete. Please use the derived fact ../stateTaxWithheld in downstream calculations.

Fact.Name: State income tax withheld
Fact.Description:
Form W-2G box 15, the state income tax withheld on this gambling winning.
COMPLETE-SAFE: $0 when the box is unanswered. That is interest:/interestReports/*/stateTaxWithheld's body exactly, and unemployment:/form1099Gs/*/stateTaxWithheld's - a return that answers nothing resolves this fact Complete $0 on every item of the collection.
NOT ROUNDED, and deliberately. There is no printed federal line under it; both shipping stateSystems-exported withholding twins in this dictionary are unrounded; and summing already-rounded per-document amounts is the known defect. A consumer that ever puts a total of these on a printed line owes the single Round at that line.
THE FEDERAL RETURN READS NOTHING FROM THIS FACT. It is export-only on the federal side and no federal line moves with it.

Fact.Name: Total W-2G gambling winnings (Schedule 1 line 8b)
Fact.Description: The sum of box-1 reportable winnings across all Forms W-2G — Schedule 1 line 8b ("Gambling. Enter gambling winnings not attributable to a trade or business."). COMPLETE-SAFE via the /alaskaPfdIncome pattern: when the /formW2Gs collection was never answered this resolves 0. Gambling LOSSES are an itemized deduction (Schedule A) and are NOT netted here — Schedule 1 line 8b carries winnings gross. Non-W-2G gambling winnings are a separate writable.

Fact.Name: Total W-2G federal income tax withheld (Form 1040 line 25c)
Fact.Description: The sum of box-4 federal withholding across all Forms W-2G — Form 1040 line 25c ("Other Forms"). COMPLETE-SAFE via the /alaskaPfdIncome pattern (0 when the collection was never answered), so /totalWithholding is unchanged when no Form W-2G is entered.

Fact.Name: Has Forms W-2G
Fact.Description:
The return reports at least one Form W-2G with reportable winnings (complete-safe: false when the collection was never answered). CONSUMED by income:/flowHasReportedIncome, and the Export below is that consumption's prerequisite, not a decoration: an Export makes a fact non-private to its module, which is what a cross-module Dependency requires (docs-upstream/adr-fact-modules.md).
THE SELF-DECLARATION THIS REPLACES said the fact was informational, not wired into the flow gates, and named /hasAlaskaPfdIncome as the precedent for leaving it that way. That citation picked the family's one outlier. The seven OTHER per-form income presence gates are all members of income:/flowHasReportedIncome and all exported: formW2s:/hasW2s, unemployment:/receivedUnemploymentCompensation, interest:/hasInterestReports, form1099Misc:/has1099Misc, cdcc:/hasReportedDependentCareBenefits, form1099Rs:/has1099R and socialSecurity:/hasSocialSecurityBenefits. The last of those is this fact's exact twin, an amount test rather than a collection size, which is why the winnings-greater-than-zero body is kept as authored instead of being restated as a CollectionSize.
AND THE PRECEDENT DOES NOT TRANSFER, for a reason worth stating: /hasAlaskaPfdIncome is redundant to that Any, not missing from it. form1099Misc:/alaskaPfd1099s is a Filter over /form1099Miscs, so an Alaska PFD IS a 1099-MISC and its section is already represented by /has1099Misc. A W-2G is its own intake collection and was represented by nothing.
THE GAP, MEASURED rather than argued: a return whose only income is W-2G winnings puts that income on Schedule 1 line 8b (via income:/otherIncome) and turns income:/requiresSchedule1 true, yet income:/flowHasReportedIncome resolved Complete FALSE. Witnessed both ways by the minimal pair tests/nodes/ty2025/formW2Gs/: case w2g-only-income-flow-gate (5,000 of winnings, every other income section answered empty) against no-w2g-no-income-flow-gate, the SAME fixture with an empty W-2G collection. The pair differs only in the W-2G, so the flip witnesses THIS membership; before it, the first case resolved false too.

Fact.Name: W-2G winnings attributable to a trade or business
Fact.Description:
Exports whether W-2G box 1 winnings are attributable to a gambling trade or business. When complete positive W-2G winnings exist, this follows the required filer attestation; when winnings are zero it is Complete False. A True answer is refused because this dictionary does not yet route the winnings and related expenses through Schedule C and Schedule SE. The income-module Schedule 1 line 8b consumer must also exclude these winnings before the refusal can be retired. Do not interpret False as proving that the filer has no gambling business income from other sources.
This fact does not itself carry the submission guard: /w2gWinningsBusinessRouteIsUnresolved names the same population affirmatively (positive winnings classified yes, with no modeled route) and carries BlockSubmissionOnTrue and the flow:/flowIsKnockedOut membership instead, because an Incomplete member of that Any would hold the whole aggregate at Placeholder for the entire positive-winnings population and hide any other knockout those returns carry. This fact remains the exported classification contract every consumer of the answer should read.

Fact.Name: Gambling trade-or-business route is unresolved (alias of the S167 refusal)
Fact.Description: Derived alias of /flowKnockoutGamblingTradeOrBusiness: True exactly when the return-level gambling classification /writableGamblesAsATradeOrBusiness is answered Yes, and complete-safe False when it is unanswered or No. It no longer blocks submission itself. RE-DEFINED: the trunk's W-2G-only question (asked only when /w2gWinnings is positive) and block 17's return-level question shared one path; the ruling keeps block 17's population, since a professional-gambler question covers winnings or losses whether or not a Form W-2G was issued, and keeps ONE refusal, the block-17 knockout, which is the flow:/flowIsKnockedOut member. This fact's former BlockSubmissionOnTrue and flow membership are removed so the return is refused once. It stays defined, with the same True/False meaning for every return that has positive W-2G winnings, because fixtures and records name it. Ruling 6 still holds: an unanswered classification never refuses.

Fact.Name: W-2G calendar year
Fact.Description: The calendar year box in the form header on the Form W-2G this winner received, recorded with fact type String on the W-2G item. The form prints the century as a fixed 20 and leaves a two digit cell, so the recorded value is the two printed digits; the box repeats identically on every copy of the document and all copies record the same year. Intake only: a faithful record of what the payer printed. IRSW2G renders once per item of /formW2Gs (includeForEach in dictionary/pdf/2025/IRSW2G/en/configuration.yml), so the printed box addresses this leaf as a starred path and every printed copy carries its own W-2G. No federal line computes from it: /w2gWinnings (Schedule 1 line 8b) and /w2gWithholding (Form 1040 line 25c) are the graph's only W-2G consumers and they read boxes 1 and 4 only.
